 Appearance:
 MS KARUNA V RAHEVAR(3818) for the Appellant(s) No. 1  for the Defendant(s) No. 2,3  MR. HIREN MODI for the Defendant(s) - claimant(s)

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant - insurance company, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 31.03.2014 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Vadodara in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1275 of 2004, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.8,16,060/-
with 9% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding opponents liable, jointly and severally.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1275 of 2004
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1
On 23.06.2004, the accident occurred.
The claimant got injured, and his left leg has been amputated.

2.2 After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding Oriental Insruance Co. Ltd vs Ashokbhai Dhanjibhai Tadvi on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199096360/

2.3 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the present appeal is preferred by the insurance company.
3. Learned advocate for the appellant - insurance company has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not properly calculating the amount of compensation.

It is submitted that amount awarded is on higer side as the Tribunal has not properly considered the various aspects;
like income of the injured, injuries, prospective income, actual loss, etc.

It is submitted that the Tribunal has committed error in considering the monthly income of the injured Rs.4,000/-, which should be Rs.2,200/- considering the fact that he was doing color work contractor and considering the fact that he has not produced any document in support of his income, and taking into account the minimum wages prevailed in the year of accident.
Accordingly, actual loss of income may be decreased considering the income of the injured.

It is submitted that considering decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Shethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, as well as taking into account the age of the injured, addition to the extent of 25% may be granted in monthly income of the injured.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Shethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that the Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation under different heads, except the above raised.
It is submitted that the appropriate enhancement be granted by modifying the award impugned.
It is submitted that the appeal may be allowed.

4. Per contra, learned advocate for respondents has submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1016/2015 ORDER DATED:
13/08/2024 undefined and proper.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has rightly considered the income of the injured.
Furthermore, in addition to the amount awarded by the Tribunal, under the head of pain, shock and suffering, special diet, attendant charges, and attendant charges, loss of amenities.
It is also submitted that no interference is required in the impugned award.
5. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimant/s.
6.1
I have heard the learned advocates for the respective parties and considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

It is noted that the claimant has by and large claimed enhancement towards income of the injured, injuries, prospective income,
actual loss, etc.
At the outset, I have considering the decision cited at the bar by learned advocate for the appellant.
The judgments cited at the bar by learned advocate for the appellant is helpful to the facts of the present case.

 6.2

sentences.text: It transpires that the Tribunal has considered the monthl income of the injured Rs.4,000/-, which should be Rs.2,200/- considering the fact that he was doing color work contractor and considering the fact that he has not produced any document in support of his income, and taking into account the minimum wages prevailed in the year of accident.

Furthermore, considering various above-mentioned judgments of the Hon'ble Apex and taking into account the age of the claimant at the time of accident, i.e., 49 years, addition to the extent of 25% is required to be granted in the monthly income.
Therefore, it would come to Rs.2,750/- towards prospective income.
It is required to take note of the fact that learned advocate for the appellant has not disputed multiplier and disability considered by the Tribunal.
Otherwise also, the Tribunal has rightly considered those aspects.
Therefore, Rs.2,750/- x 80% x 12 (annual) x 13 (multiplier) would come to Rs.3,43,200/- which would be the future loss of income of the claimant.
6.3 Furthermore, actual loss of income should be Rs.13,200/-, instead of Rs.24,000/- considering the monthly income Rs.2,200/- of the claimant for six months.

Furthermore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Syed Sadiq vs. United India Insurance Company Ltd. reported in (2014) 2 SCC 735, the compensation under the heads of pain, shock and suffering, special diet,
attendant charges and transportation and future medical expenses would be increased to the extent 1,50,000/-, 50,000/- and 50,000/- respectively.

7. Therefore, I hold that the claimant/s are entitled to get the total amount of compensation of Rs.6,61,500/- with 9% p.a. interest from the date of filing the claim petition till its realisation, which would meet the ends of justice.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal shall remain same.
The Tribunal has already awarded Rs.8,16,060/- and, therefore, amount of Rs.1,54,560/- would be refunded to the insurance company by the Tribunal.
8. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
8.1 The present appeal is allowed to the aforesaid extent.

8.2 The impugned judgment and award dated 31.03.2014 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Vadodara in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1275 of 2004 is modified to the aforesaid extent.
